justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Once certified, analysts almost universally remain in informatics/IT roles; attrition back to bedside is rare given the pay delta and Epic's hiring pipeline.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Epic certifications are the single most-requested EHR credential in U.S. health-system, consultancy, and Epic-corporate job postings.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Mid-career Epic analysts earn $100K-$150K and senior consultants $160K-$220K, a clear premium over same-tenure clinical PT/OT salaries.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Build certs teach real configuration, Chronicles data model, and workflow design; meaningful technical depth, though not full software-engineering rigor.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Clinicians with workflow expertise are explicitly recruited as application analysts; PT/OT background maps cleanly to Rehab/Therapy or Ambulatory modules.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Cert itself is short (weeks) and Epic-funded, but it is gated by first landing an Epic-shop hire, so end-to-end accessibility is low.
